articles.summary: Today, the Supreme Court will hear arguments in Watson v. Republican National Committee, a case with signiﬁcant implications for mail voting in more than a dozen states. The case centers on a Mississippi law that allows mail-in ballots postmarked on or before Election Day to be counted if they are received within ﬁve business days after Election Day.
articles.title: Vote.org Statement on Watson v. Republican National Committee

articles.summary: As Senate Debates SAVE Act, Nation's Largest Voting Organization Calls on Senators to Vote No
articles.title: Vote.org Urges Senate to Reject Restrictive, Antidemocratic Voting Bill

articles.summary: Vote.org today responded to the Florida Legislature’s passage of HB 991, a bill that would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote and restrict the forms of identiﬁcation accepted at the polls. The bill now heads to Governor Ron DeSantis, who is expected to sign it into law.
articles.title: Vote.org Statement on Florida HB 991: 872,000 Voters at Risk of Disenfranchisement

articles.summary: Vote.org CEO Andrea Hailey issued the following statement after the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Arkansas cannot require voters to use a handwritten signature to register to vote, blocking a rule that effectively banned online voter registration tools in the state. Vote.org was a plaintiff in the case.
articles.title: Vote.org Applauds Federal Appeals Court for Key Voting Rights Decision
